name: 625-batchdecode-llama3-8b-1gpu
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, bf16, ~16 GB of weights. An ungated re-upload of the Meta repository of the same weights, which is gated.
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one node, one GPU.
parallelism: tp1. No tensor, pipeline, expert or data parallelism.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM, 8B dense, 32 layers, GQA 32:8, head_dim 128, 8192-token window; the rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 1500 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix: prompts 1024 +- 128 (clamped 768-1280) and generations 256 +- 32 (clamped 192-320), streamed to /v1/completions rather than the chat route, seed 42.
purpose: An 8B chat assistant streaming paragraph-length replies to 32 concurrent users from a single H100 GPU.
launch:
# sglang at commit 5ac8b80677614a9c024740e94f9a087a39eb3499 (`git describe --tags` =
# v0.1.20-4-g5ac8b806776), launched from the interpreter named in configs/env.yaml.
#
# Flat `key: value` only. A nested block is DROPPED by the flat parser and the engine then
# runs without the mechanism this file declares.

model-path: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
tp-size: 1
mem-fraction-static: 0.85

# The dataclass default at this commit is 8, i.e. one SSE chunk per eight generated tokens,
# which would make the inter-token metric a chunk cadence rather than a token cadence.
stream-interval: 1

random-seed: 42

# CUDA graphs and the flashinfer attention path are left ON, which is the engine default and
# is the declared operating point. Do NOT reach for --disable-flashinfer: init_cuda_graphs
# returns None on either flag, so it silently turns CUDA graphs off as well.
